requirements.requirement: Planter suitable for a sunny kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Linear 3-cell build (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full + piece:-1,0,0;full) total ~3 hexes long, windowsill-scale compact footprint; bins are full-depth planters with soil.
Three bins each filled with soil and planted: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full with basil-young, bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full with mint-young, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full with parsley-young (prop:1,2,3 visible)

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell linear windowsill planter with three full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with a different herb (basil, mint, parsley). Compact size suits a sunny kitchen windowsill, capped and bolted for stability, plants clearly visible.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Sunny kitchen sill, three fresh herbs — I'll assemble your planter now.
